response.sql: WITH baseline AS (SELECT AVG(instownpct) AS baseline_avg FROM sentimentandfundamentals WHERE instownpct IS NOT NULL), group_averages AS (SELECT COALESCE(eventannotm, 'MISSING') AS timing_group, AVG(instownpct) AS group_avg FROM sentimentandfundamentals GROUP BY COALESCE(eventannotm, 'MISSING')), above_baseline AS (SELECT ga.group_avg, b.baseline_avg FROM group_averages ga CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE ga.group_avg > b.baseline_avg) SELECT AVG(group_avg) AS mean_of_averages, AVG(group_avg - baseline_avg) AS mean_excess_over_baseline FROM above_baseline;

assumptions.assumption: "Mean of their averages" refers to simple arithmetic mean of qualifying group averages, not weighted by group size. The phrase "larger groups weigh more" contextually explains the baseline calculation method (using all individual snapshots) rather than prescribing weighting for the final output calculation.

alternatives.interpretation: If "larger groups weigh more" also applies to the final output calculations, weight each group's average by its count of non-NULL instownpct values when computing both the mean of averages and the mean excess.
alternatives.sql: WITH baseline AS (SELECT AVG(instownpct) AS baseline_avg FROM sentimentandfundamentals WHERE instownpct IS NOT NULL), group_stats AS (SELECT COALESCE(eventannotm, 'MISSING') AS timing_group, AVG(instownpct) AS group_avg, COUNT(CASE WHEN instownpct IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS group_size FROM sentimentandfundamentals GROUP BY COALESCE(eventannotm, 'MISSING')), above_baseline AS (SELECT ga.group_avg, ga.group_size, b.baseline_avg FROM group_stats ga CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE ga.group_avg > b.baseline_avg) SELECT SUM(group_avg * group_size) / SUM(group_size) AS mean_of_averages, SUM((group_avg - baseline_avg) * group_size) / SUM(group_size) AS mean_excess_over_baseline FROM above_baseline;
